correctness.rationale: The pointwise recurrence A u_t=r(u_{t-1}+u_{t+1}) follows rigorously from saturated contact budgets and disjoint refractory phases on any periodic orbit. Fourier modes map to integral adjacency eigenvalues, forcing temporal root-of-unity orders 1,2,3,4,6; hence all state periods divide 12. Refractory exclusion eliminates 1/2 periodic excitations; eigenvalue exclusion at -r,0,r leaves only these modes, proving extinction. Sharp witnesses and nonintegral boundary checked with direct state iteration. SRG spectra independently derived by exact arithmetic from standard documented parameters; no partial enumeration is substituted for the infinite proof. A third independent integer-state checker verifies the saturated contact identity at every recurrent state and phase of the small example graphs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The published general geometric-contraction bound needs threshold strictly greater than half maximum degree, whereas the new theorem operates at equality. The 2016 arbitrary-graph theorem uses one-neighbor contact, not variable half-degree. The tripartite result has fixed threshold two and is not a superset of all integral regular graphs. Doba (2018) also explicitly uses one-neighbor excitation and is not a higher critical-threshold theorem.

The inspected half-degree theorem establishes only immediate three-cycles, not a period-twelve global bound; the tripartite census is restricted to tripartite graphs; strict threshold-above-half extinction excludes the critical equality. This result covers arbitrary integral even-regular graphs and critical extinction on triangle-free Gewirtz and Higman-Sims graphs. Historical-priority uncertainty is explicit.

value.rationale: A graph-wide, all-period, sharp temporal bound from integrality is a structural dynamical theorem, not a textbook finite census. Its spectral exclusion settles universal extinction at a critical contact value on two canonical triangle-free integral strongly regular graphs, which the earlier triangle-based three-cycle and strict-threshold decay results cannot treat. The disjoint C3 and C4 sharp witness and nonintegral C5 boundary show exactness and necessity of hypothesis for a general statement.
